# Overview

This file reads the two annotated workbooks independently, attaches **one cluster assignment per participant from the corresponding experiment × condition cluster CSV**, and conducts **separate** analyses for four groups:

1. Experiment 1 — Curvature instruction
2. Experiment 1 — No instruction
3. Experiment 2 — Curvature instruction
4. Experiment 2 — No instruction

For each group, **human and AI coding are shown separately** and compared for agreement. Only five binary indicators are analyzed. **Priority 1–3**, **notes**, and the Experiment 2 **animal-like** indicator are reserved for later analyses. Missing indicator codes are preserved as `NA`, not recoded as zero.

**File placement:** Put this `.Rmd` and both Excel workbooks in `OOO_Curvature/Open_Answer_Analysis/`. Leave the four `participant_cluster_lookup.csv` files where the main analyses exported them. This `.Rmd` accesses them at these *relative paths*:

- `../Exp1/Exp1_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp1/Exp1_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp2/Exp2_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp2/Exp2_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`

The relative paths are resolved from the `.Rmd` directory when knitting in RStudio. The human workbook has four study sheets; the AI workbook has those same four sheets plus a `Coding guide`, which is not used.

The current workbooks contain **35, 36, 36 and 36** participants, respectively, for a total of **143 distinct IDs**. Participant IDs are unique across the four experiment–condition groups. Some rows without participant IDs are continuation text, **not additional participants**.

# Setup and data import

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.8)
```


```{r}
library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

human_file <- "Curvature Open Answers.xlsx"
ai_file <- "Curvature_Open_Answers_AI.xlsx"

stopifnot(file.exists(human_file), file.exists(ai_file))
```

## Import all excel four sheets 
```{r}
normalize_id <- function(x) {
  sub("\\.0+$", "", trimws(as.character(x)))
}

binary_code <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[is.na(x) | x == ""] <- NA_character_

  if (any(!is.na(x) & !(x %in% c("0", "1")))) {
    stop("A coding column contains a value other than 0, 1, or NA.")
  }

  as.integer(x)
}


read_answers <- function(file, sheet, experiment, condition, coder) {

  dat <- read_excel(file, sheet = sheet, col_types = "text")

  if (experiment == "Exp 2") {

    # Exp2 has 6 indicators (columns 3–8)
    dat <- dat[, 1:9]

    names(dat) <- c(
      "subj_id", "answer", "smoothness", "vertices",
      "third_feature", "intuition", "globalness", "animal_like", "size"
    )

  } else {

    # Exp1 has 5 indicators (columns 3–7)
    dat <- dat[, 1:8]

    names(dat) <- c(
      "subj_id", "answer", "smoothness", "vertices",
      "third_feature", "intuition", "globalness", "size"
    )

    dat$animal_like <- NA_character_
  }

  dat %>%
    filter(!is.na(subj_id), trimws(subj_id) != "") %>%
    mutate(
      subj_id = normalize_id(subj_id),
      across(c(smoothness:animal_like, size), binary_code),
      experiment = experiment,
      condition = condition,
      coder = coder,
      .before = 1
    )
}

# Human coding
human <- bind_rows(
  read_answers(human_file, "exp1 curv",
               "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp1 noInstr",
               "Exp 1", "No instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp2 curv",
               "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp2 noInstr",
               "Exp 2", "No instruction", "Human")
)

# AI coding
ai <- bind_rows(
  read_answers(ai_file, "exp1 curv",
               "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction", "AI"),
  read_answers(ai_file, "exp1 noInstr",
               "Exp 1", "No instruction", "AI"),
  read_answers(ai_file, "exp2 curv",
               "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction", "AI"),
  read_answers(ai_file, "exp2 noInstr",
               "Exp 2", "No instruction", "AI")
)

answers <- bind_rows(human, ai)

# Check number of participants per group and coder
answers %>%
  count(experiment, condition, coder, name = "n_participants")
```

## Checking participant IDs
```{r}
# Check for duplicates
duplicates <- answers %>%
  count(experiment, condition, coder, subj_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(duplicates)
stopifnot(nrow(duplicates) == 0)

# Check human and AI participant coverage
keys <- c("experiment", "condition", "subj_id")

human_ids <- human %>% select(all_of(keys))
ai_ids <- ai %>% select(all_of(keys))

only_human <- anti_join(human_ids, ai_ids, by = keys)
only_ai <- anti_join(ai_ids, human_ids, by = keys)

print(only_human)
print(only_ai)

stopifnot(
  nrow(only_human) == 0,
  nrow(only_ai) == 0
)
```

## import cluster info
```{r}
read_clusters <- function(file, experiment, condition) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) stop("Missing cluster CSV: ", file)

  dat <- read_csv(
    file,
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  if (!all(c("subj_id", "cluster") %in% names(dat))) {
    stop("Cluster CSV needs subj_id and cluster: ", file)
  }

  dat %>%
    transmute(
      experiment = experiment,
      condition = condition,
      subj_id = normalize_id(subj_id),
      cluster = trimws(as.character(cluster))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(subj_id), subj_id != "") %>%
    distinct()
}

cluster_lookup <- bind_rows(
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp1/Exp1_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp1/Exp1_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 1", "No instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp2/Exp2_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp2/Exp2_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 2", "No instruction"
  )
)

# Number of participants in each cluster
cluster_lookup %>%
  count(experiment, condition, cluster, name = "n_participants")

```
## Check and join the cluster assignments
```{r}
# Check for conflicting cluster assignments
cluster_duplicates <- cluster_lookup %>%
  count(experiment, condition, subj_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(cluster_duplicates)
stopifnot(nrow(cluster_duplicates) == 0)

# Check for missing cluster labels in the lookup
stopifnot(
  !any(is.na(cluster_lookup$cluster) | cluster_lookup$cluster == "")
)

# Identify participants without a cluster match
missing_clusters <- answers %>%
  distinct(experiment, condition, subj_id) %>%
  anti_join(cluster_lookup, by = keys)

print(missing_clusters)

# Join cluster assignments
answers_all <- answers %>%
  left_join(cluster_lookup, by = keys)

# Keep only participants with clusters for cluster-based analyses
answers_clustered <- answers_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster), cluster != "")

if (nrow(missing_clusters) > 0) {
  warning(
    nrow(missing_clusters),
    " participant(s) lack cluster assignments. Verify them in the main analysis."
  )
}

# Check final numbers by cluster
answers_clustered %>%
  distinct(experiment, condition, subj_id, cluster) %>%
  count(experiment, condition, cluster, name = "n_participants")
```

## Prepare the five features and check missing coding values
```{r}
answers_long_all <- answers_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      smoothness, vertices, third_feature,
      intuition, globalness, animal_like, size
    ),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "mentioned"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    feature = case_when(
      feature == "smoothness" ~ "Smoothness",
      feature == "vertices" ~ "Vertices",
      feature == "third_feature" & experiment == "Exp 1" ~ "Angle",
      feature == "third_feature" & experiment == "Exp 2" ~ "Range",
      feature == "intuition" ~ "Intuition",
      feature == "globalness" ~ "Globalness",
      feature == "animal_like" ~ "Animal-like",
      feature == "size" ~ "Size"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(experiment == "Exp 1" & feature == "Animal-like")
  )

# Check missing indicator codes
missing_codes <- answers_long_all %>%
  group_by(experiment, condition, coder, feature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_missing = sum(is.na(mentioned)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_missing > 0)

print(missing_codes)

# Dataset for cluster analyses
answers_long <- answers_long_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster), cluster != "")
```

## Feature mention rates by cluster
```{r}
mention_rates <- answers_long %>%
  group_by(experiment, condition, coder, cluster, feature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_coded = sum(!is.na(mentioned)),
    n_mentioned = sum(mentioned == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = if_else(
      n_coded > 0,
      n_mentioned / n_coded,
      NA_real_
    ),
    percentage = 100 * proportion
  )

# 95% Wilson confidence intervals
z <- qnorm(0.975)

mention_rates <- mention_rates %>%
  mutate(
    denominator = 1 + z^2 / n_coded,
    center = (proportion + z^2 / (2 * n_coded)) / denominator,
    half_width = z * sqrt(
      proportion * (1 - proportion) / n_coded +
      z^2 / (4 * n_coded^2)
    ) / denominator,
    ci_lower = 100 * pmax(0, center - half_width),
    ci_upper = 100 * pmin(1, center + half_width)
  ) %>%
  select(-denominator, -center, -half_width)

# Save descriptive results
dir.create("open_answer_outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(
  mention_rates,
  "open_answer_outputs/mention_rates.csv"
)
```

```{r}

  ) %>%
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggh4x)

# Consistent project colors
feature_cols <- c(
  "Smoothness" = "#F8766D",
  "Vertices" = "#00BA38",
  "Angle" = "#619CFF",
  "Range" = "#619CFF",
  "Intuition" = "#A78BFA",
  "Globalness" = "#B59B73",
  "Animal-like" = "#CC79A7",
  "Size" = "#E69F00"
)

plot_open_answers <- function(exp, cond) {

  dat <- mention_rates %>%
    filter(
      experiment == exp,
      condition == cond
    )
  
  cluster_ns <- answers_clustered %>%
    filter(
      experiment == exp,
      condition == cond
    ) %>%
    distinct(subj_id, cluster) %>%
    count(cluster, name = "n_participants")

  # Set the correct features for each experiment
  feature_order <- if (exp == "Exp 1") {
    c("Smoothness", "Vertices", "Angle",
      "Intuition", "Globalness", "Size")
  } else {
    c("Smoothness", "Vertices", "Range",
      "Intuition", "Globalness", "Animal-like", "Size")
  }

  # Set cluster order
  clusters <- sort(unique(as.character(dat$cluster)))
  
  # Add n to cluster labels
  cluster_labels_df <- tibble(cluster = clusters) %>%
    left_join(cluster_ns, by = "cluster") %>%
    mutate(
      strip_label = paste0(cluster, " (n = ", n_participants, ")")
    )
  
  cluster_labels <- setNames(
    cluster_labels_df$strip_label,
    cluster_labels_df$cluster
  )
  
  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(
      feature = factor(feature, levels = feature_order),
      cluster = factor(cluster, levels = clusters, labels = cluster_labels[clusters]),
      coder = factor(coder, levels = c("Human", "AI"))
    )
  
  # Colored cluster headings
  cluster_colors <- ifelse(
    grepl("smooth", clusters, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "#F8766D", "#00BA38"
  )
  
  cluster_fills <- ifelse(
    grepl("smooth", clusters, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "#FDE8E6", "#E8F7EC"
  )
  cluster_strip <- ggh4x::strip_themed(
    background_x = ggh4x::elem_list_rect(
      fill = cluster_fills,
      colour = rep("black", length(clusters)),
      linewidth = rep(0.6, length(clusters))
    ),
    text_x = ggh4x::elem_list_text(
      colour = cluster_colors,
      face = rep("bold", length(clusters)),
      size = rep(12, length(clusters))
    )
  )

  # Figure
  ggplot(
    dat,
    aes(
      x = feature,
      y = percentage,
      fill = feature
    )
  ) +

    geom_col(
      width = 0.65,
      alpha = 0.65,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +

    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = ci_lower,
        ymax = ci_upper
      ),
      width = 0.15,
      linewidth = 0.5,
      color = "black"
    ) +

    ggh4x::facet_grid2(
      rows = vars(coder),
      cols = vars(cluster),
      strip = cluster_strip,
      axes = "x",
      remove_labels = "x"
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(values = feature_cols) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
      limits = c(0, 100),
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +

    labs(
      x = "Feature mentioned",
      y = "Participants mentioning feature (%)",
      title = paste(exp, "—", cond)
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 35,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 10
      ),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(12, "pt"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        color = "grey92",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 16,
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
}
```

```{r}

  "Exp 1",
  "Curvature instruction"
)

print(p_exp1_curv)
```

# Word Frequencies

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
# install.packages('ggwordcloud')
library(ggwordcloud)
library(tibble)

word_freq <- tibble(
  term = c(
    "sharpness", "curved", "smoothness", "pointiness",
    "roundness", "straight", "softness", "hard",
    "corner", "curvature", "curviness", "zigzag",
    "pointy", "curve", "brash", "harshness",
    "peaks", "triangle-like", "wave", "jagged",
    "tips", "continuous", "spikes", "angle",
    "rigidity"
  ),
  frequency = c(
    19, 13, 7, 7, 6, 6, 4, 2, 2, 2, 2,
    rep(1, 14)
  )
)

# Verify total and inspect table
stopifnot(sum(word_freq$frequency) == 84)

print(word_freq, n = Inf)



set.seed(123)

p_wordcloud <- ggplot(
  word_freq,
  aes(
    label = term,
    size = frequency,
    color = frequency
  )
) +
  ggwordcloud::geom_text_wordcloud_area(
    rm_outside = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_area(
    max_size = 60
  ) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "#FBC8C4",
    high = "#D94B42"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(p_wordcloud)

ggsave(
  "smoothness_wordcloud.png",
  plot = p_wordcloud,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# exp2
```{r}

```
